crs.input_georeference: GeoPDF /VP /Measure: 4 corner GPTS + LPTS, Plate Carree data frame
crs.note: The declared GCS is the ArcGIS "assumed geographic" placeholder (it even names NAD27, a North American datum).  The degrees it carries are the map graticule and are WGS84-consistent: the national boundary agrees with Natural Earth to +0.25/+0.04 km and the rivers to -0.9/+0.5 km.  A literal NAD27->WGS84 transform would be wrong here (NAD27 is not defined in Nigeria).  The printed meridian labels sit 0.172 deg west of the /VP graticule lines; the /VP values are used (the labels are a typographic offset, and the /VP choice is confirmed by the two checks above).

features: coastline / sea edge (raster of the map sheet)

model.note: dlat = (A + B*(lat-lat0)) / km_per_deg degrees, north positive; dlon = 0

notes: The 2023 sheet is a GeoPDF whose raster basemap (and the rivers/roads/railway/symbols
drawn over it) is out of register with its own /VP frame by several km, while its text
(towns, states, river names, mineral numbers), the national boundary and the town
markers are in register -- text-to-text against the 2011 sheet: +0.1 km E, +1.1 km N.
The 2011 sheet agrees with Natural Earth to ~1 km everywhere, so only the raster-derived
content of the 2023 sheet is corrected.  Measured against NE: 2023 coastline 7.6 km south
(2011: 0.4 km), capitals 6.8 km south (2011: 1.0 km), linework 5.0 km south of 2011.

topographic_overlay.note: The sheets' topographic overlay (towns, roads, railway, capital squares) was plotted with a ~0.66 % scale error relative to the graticule.  This model measures that displacement; it is NOT applied to the layers. Corrected town coordinates are in towns_true_wgs84.csv.  See ACCURACY.md section 4.3.
